ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), Act No. 6510 (Nov. 28, 2001), as amended, including Articles 2 (beneficial owner definition), 5 (customer due diligence), 7 (suspicious transaction reporting), 8 (currency transaction reporting), 12 (record keeping), 31 (confidentiality) and 32 (sanctions); Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality, Act No. 5493 (Jan. 13, 1998), Articles 3 and 4; Financial Services Commission Regulations on Customer Identification and Verification; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) administrative rules. South Korea maintains no publicly accessible centralized UBO registry; beneficial ownership information is verified by financial institutions and reported on a government-only-access basis to the FSC/KoFIU and other competent supervisory authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registration Certificate / certified corporate registry extract of the Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office (IROS) of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in a Hague Apostille member state: obtain a certified corporate registry extract from the Korean registry court; authenticate it as required by a Korean notary public; obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; deliver the document directly and do not add any consular legalization. For use in a non-Hague state: obtain the certified extract; notarize; obtain Korean MOFA authentication; then submit the document to the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the destination country for consular legalization. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence / Tax Compliance Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea or, for a foreign parent entity, the competent corporate registry or tax authority of the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: have the issuing authority or a notary attest the responsible official's signature; obtain an Apostille from the relevant central authority (Korean MOFA for Korean documents; Secretary of State, FCDO, or equivalent for foreign documents); submit directly without consular legalization. Non-Hague path: notarize the certificate; obtain authentication from the issuing state's foreign ministry or competent authority; obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea's Embassy/Consulate having jurisdiction; never add an Apostille to a consularized document or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing the local registered agent or the designated attorney-in-fact to execute incorporation filings and open the corporate bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the shareholder/UBO-pierced entity (or sole shareholder resolution of the Chusik Hoesa pre-incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille states: execute the resolution or power of attorney in accordance with the corporate seal/bylaw certification rules; have a notary public certify the director's signature; obtain an Apostille from the competent authority in the state of execution; use directly in Korea. Non-Apostille states: notarize; obtain foreign ministry authentication; obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy/Consulate in the executing state; simultaneously, if the beneficiary authority is in Korea, the Korean MOFA may require further authentication. Apostille and consular legalization are alternatives, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeonggwan) of the Chusik Hoesa, including the corporate purpose, authorized capital, share structure, board composition and UBO disclosure annex
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founders and incorporating notary public in South Korea; certified copy registered with the Supreme Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille-era destination: after filing, obtain a certified copy from the Korean registry court; notarize the conformity of the certified copy; request an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular legalization is required. For a non-Apostille destination: certified copy from the registry court; notarize; obtain MOFA authentication; obtain consular legalization from the destination country's Embassy in Seoul; never combine an Apostille with consular legalization in the same authentication chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (account conduct and UBO due-diligence letter from the shareholder's or the target's relationship bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A regulated banking institution, e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, Hana or the UBO's home-country relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: bank letter on bank letterhead signed by an authorized branch manager; notarize the manager's signature in the country of issuance; obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority; present to the Korean bank or registry user as a standalone authentication. Non-Apostille path: notarize the bank manager's signature; obtain authentication from the issuing state's central authority; obtain Korean consular legalization; the document may then be presented in Korea. Under no circumstances should a document that has received an Apostille subsequently be routed for consular legalization, as the two regimes are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting the engagement, identify and verify every individual ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of issued shares or effective voting control, plus all directors, officers and authorized signatories. Screen continuously against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN/SSI and sectoral sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, UK OFSI consolidated list, Korean FSC/KoFIU designated lists, FATF public statements on high-risk jurisdictions, and domestic law-enforcement watchlists. Screen for domestic and foreign PEP status under FATF Recommendation 12, including family members and close associates; if a PEP is identified, apply enhanced due diligence, obtain independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, and require senior management approval before onboarding. All screening results, evidence of UBO verification, and customer files must be maintained under FTRA Article 12 for at least seven years and be available to KoFIU, the Financial Supervisory Service and external auditors.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Registry Office (IROS) - Internet Registration Service (www.iros.go.kr); foreign-invested enterprise integration through KOTRA/STARTBIZ and the Korean Commercial Registry of the competent district court
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the legal trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be written in Hangul and must contain the corporate-form identifier 'Chusik Hoesa' or a permissible abbreviation. A foreign-language name may be used only as a secondary trade name; the statutory registered name in the court registry is the Hangul name. The mandatory four-tier naming convention is: (i) a distinct identifying trade name

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288, 289, 295, 305, 312, 316, 317, 329, 393 and 435; Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 10471, as amended), Articles 12 through 25; Foreign Investment Promotion Act for foreign-invested enterprise status; Value-Added Tax Act and Corporate Tax Act for post-registration tax obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court exercising jurisdiction over the company's registered office; in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office, with electronic filing accepted through the Supreme Court IROS (Internet Registration Office System).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration under the Commercial Registration Act (IROS statutory form or paper form prescribed by the Supreme Court), together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and all required attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; incorporators may determine a nominal capital amount. However, the full subscription price must be deposited into a bank-designated incorporation escrow or share subscription deposit account before filing the registration application, and the bank deposit certificate must be attached to the incorporation filing. For a foreign investor seeking foreign direct investment recognition under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the investment must generally meet the KRW 100 million threshold and be reported to the Foreign Investment Ombudsman/KOTRA procedures; otherwise no blocked escrow minimum applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CORPORATE NAME], a Chusik Hoesa organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea. Date: [DATE]; Venue: Registered Office; Present: all incumbent directors. WHEREAS the incorporators have subscribed to and fully paid the issued capital before this meeting and have lodged the bank deposit certificate with the company; WHEREAS the Board plans to adopt its statutory registered office, authorize corporate banking arrangements, subscribe and allot shares, and appoint statutory officers; WHEREAS management authority is vested in the Board pursuant to Article 393 of the Korean Commercial Act. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The Board confirms the total issued capital is KRW [AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] fully paid ordinary shares. The Board ratifies the subscription and allotment to each subscriber named in the subscription ledger, and declares that the full subscription amount has been deposited into a designated capital deposit account at [BANK] in compliance with Article 295 of the Commercial Act. The Board instructs the Representative Director to issue share certificates and to maintain the shareholder ledger at the registered office. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes opening operating, reserve, and settlement accounts at [BANK] and authorizes the Representative Director, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Compliance Officer as authorized signatories, with dual-signature controls for any transaction exceeding [THRESHOLD]. The Board ratifies the onboarding of PayPal and Stripe payment rails for customer-support SaaS subscriptions, subject to anti-money-laundering verification and banking consent. Bank forms and counterparty authorization documents may be executed in original or electronic form. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board approves the office located at [ADDRESS], Republic of Korea as the registered office and principal place of business for service of legal process, tax notification, and statutory correspondence. The Board directs the corporate secretary to record the registered office in the Commercial Registry and with the National Tax Service. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [NAME] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [NAME] as Director and Chief Financial Officer, [NAME] as Director and Compliance Officer, and [NAME] as Corporate Secretary. Each officer shall perform statutory duties with care, loyalty, information-security diligence, and regulatory disclosure as required under the Commercial Act and the Personal Information Protection Act. 5. INDUSTRIAL AND PHYSICAL LICENSING DETERMINATION: The Board determines that ISIC 6201 customer support helpdesk and related cloud software services are purely digital and do not require an industrial manufacturing license, an Environmental Impact Assessment, or a Civil Defense special fire permit. The Board directs the Corporate Secretary to verify EIA exemption and to obtain the standard office occupancy and workplace safety clearances required by applicable building and occupational safety regulations. This resolution is final, binding, and effective upon adoption by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preliminary Company Name Clearance and Business Scope Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court / Supreme Court IROS online name search and reservation system (www.iros.go.kr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating attorney shall log into the Korean commercial registration name-search portal and validate that the proposed Korean name and English rendering are not identical or confusingly similar to any existing corporation, limited company, or registered trademark in the same business category. The business purpose clause must be drafted in Korean and English to describe only digital activities such as customer support helpdesk software, SaaS platform operation, cloud telephony, chatbot services, technical support, and data consulting, without any language implying manufacturing, chemical processing, physical warehousing, or assembly. If a foreign-name business identifier is desired, the corporate agent will reserve that name in the same application. Any proposed name containing prohibited national or public-interest terms must be rejected immediately. The filing is submitted online with statutory forms, and the clearance certificate is retained for the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation application form
Proposed Articles of Incorporation draft with English business-purpose translation
Identification documents of each incorporator and intended director
Power of attorney or authorization letter if filing through a corporate agent
Name-search and preliminary registration service fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name-search application is queried or rejected because of conflicting registrations, the attorney shall promptly select an alternate available name and file a corrected name-clearance application within one business day. No substantive deficiency arises if the applicant resubmits with a non-conflicting name. If the registry requests additional identity verification, the incorporators shall provide apostilled or notarized identification and a revised power of attorney within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Capital Subscription Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public commissioned by the local District Court, and a commercial bank branch in Korea authorized to receive the incorporation subscription deposit under Article 295 of the Commercial Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorneys shall finalize the Articles of Incorporation in Korean as the binding legal instrument, including the company name, registered office, business purpose, authorized share capital, par value, share classes, board composition, and provisions for annual audits. Each incorporator shall execute the subscription form and pay or wire the full subscription amount into a temporary incorporation escrow account opened at the designated bank. The bank shall issue a deposit certificate showing the payer, amount, date, and account description, because the Commercial Registry will accept no incorporation without proof of full capital payment. After the deposit is verified, the incorporators shall appear before a notary, verify identity, sign the articles in the notary's presence, and receive notarized certified copies. In parallel, the incorporators shall hold the constitutive meeting and execute minutes appointing the initial directors and statutory auditor where required.
required_dossiers: Final Articles of Incorporation signed by all incorporators
Share subscription application form signed by each subscriber
Bank deposit certificate evidencing full paid-in capital payment
Constitutive meeting minutes appointing directors
Notarization fee receipt
Identity certificates and registration certificates for incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses notarization due to incomplete legal-capacity verification, the incorporators must provide valid passports, alien registration cards, corporate resolutions, or court-appointed guardian documents and reschedule the notarial appointment within two business days. If the bank returns the capital deposit for regulatory reasons, the attorney shall open a new account at another licensed bank and re-execute the deposit and notarization cycle without altering the capital amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Registration with the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the local District Court, through physical submission or the Supreme Court IROS electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporate agent shall prepare the statutory Application for Corporate Registration, attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, constitutive meeting minutes, consent letters from directors, and other required evidence, and file the complete dossier with the competent Commercial Registration Office. The registry will examine the legality of the corporate purpose, the capital contribution, the registered office, and the appointment of directors. If filing in person, the representative director must present identification and the corporate registration fee payment receipt. If filing online, the representative or attorney shall use a certified digital certificate and attach all required scanned documents. Once approved, the registrar assigns a unique registration number and issues a certified Certificate of Corporate Registration. The company becomes a legal personality on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Corporate Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Constitutive meeting minutes
Consent letters signed by all appointed directors
Copies of identity documents of directors and incorporators
Corporate seal impression certificate or seal declaration
Registration tax and education tax payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementation order identifying missing or defective documents, the applicant shall submit the corrected dossier within fourteen days; the commercial registration action is otherwise treated as withdrawn. If the application is rejected, the attorney shall analyze the rejection grounds, correct the legal or documentary defect, and file a new application with a fresh fee. An appeal can be brought under the Administrative Litigation Act if the registry refuses a valid filing, but in practice resubmitting with full legal compliance is the fastest remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Registration, Business Registration, and Social Insurance Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service; local municipality or district office for local tax registration; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Workers Compensation Insurance administration offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the date of incorporation, the CFO shall file a corporate business registration application with the National Tax Service, selecting corporate income tax, VAT registration, and electronic tax-invoice issuance. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate containing the company's unique business registration number. The company must also register its payroll and employment relationships with the four major social insurance systems for directors and employees, compute monthly withholding, and prepare annual corporate tax filings. For cross-border SaaS customer support sales through PayPal or Stripe, the company shall maintain revenue reports, subscriber contracts, and platform payout histories to support VAT and corporate tax treatment. The company must also create the statutory corporate records book and notify the tax office if the company does not engage in manufacturing, thereby avoiding any industrial or environmental licensing registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration from the District Court
Business registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease contract or ownership evidence
Corporate bank account opening certificate
Director identification and foreign-address information if applicable
Digital certificate for electronic tax filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service questions the business purpose or requests a site inspection, the CFO shall submit the ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210 mapping together with a written business description confirming the digital nature of the company. If the business registration is delayed, the company may submit a voluntary retroactive application; tax penalties may be reduced by filing before any formal notice. If the social insurance authorities assess overdue premiums, the company shall pay the overdue amount and request a payment plan through the relevant regional office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Registration, Bank Account Activation, and Operational Licensing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office for corporate seal certificate; a licensed commercial bank for the corporate operating account; National Tax Service for tax filing credentials; no industrial licensing authority is triggered for ISIC 6201 digital services.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporate seal shall be registered with the District Court Commercial Registration Office, and the attorney shall obtain an original corporate seal certificate. With that certificate, the representative director shall open the corporate operating bank account at the chosen bank, providing the corporate registration certificate, business registration certificate, board resolution, signatories' identification, and the corporate seal certificate. The bank will perform customer due diligence under the Financial Transactions and Information Act and will activate the settlement account for PayPal and Stripe payouts. The company shall then confirm in writing that no manufacturing, chemical, or warehouse license is required and that no Environmental Impact Assessment report is applicable. For the physical office, the company shall obtain the standard office fire-safety inspection certificate required by the Fire Safety Act and the basic workplace safety compliance certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The corporate secretary shall finalize the corporate minute book and maintain a regulatory permit register.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal certificate issued by the District Court
Certificate of Corporate Registration
Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Board resolution authorizing the open corporate bank account and online payment rails
Signatories' identification documents
Registered office lease and building owner consent
Personal Information Protection Act privacy policy and data-processing documentation
Office fire-safety and workplace safety certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, the company must provide the source of funds, beneficial ownership declaration, evidence of the registered business, and platform contracts; a refusal may be escalated through the bank's compliance committee. If any municipal inspection mistakenly raises an industrial-license question, the company shall submit the Korean and English business description, the ISIC 6201 classification, and the tax registration certificate demonstrating that no physical manufacturing operation exists.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; ISIC 6201 is classified as an information technology service, and the company does not operate a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility. The Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act does not mandate a factory license or industrial site filing for a digital customer-support helpdesk SaaS business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; there is no specialized Korean operating license, factory establishment permit, or industrial manufacturing registration for ISIC 6201 customer support helpdesk software.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and its designated environmental assessment authorities are not required to review or register this business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable; the activity does not meet any threshold or scope of the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act, the Water Environment Conservation Act, or the Clean Air Conservation Act for requiring an EIA report or an environmental registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the company generates no process wastewater, no industrial VOC emissions, no hazardous chemical discharges, and no manufacturing waste streams. The only permitted impacts are ordinary municipal domestic use from an office environment, which remains below any regulatory threshold and requires no environmental permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable; no Special Civil Defense fire permit is required for pure digital SaaS operations. The company must nevertheless obtain a standard office fire-safety inspection certificate under the Fire Safety Act for its registered office, comply with the Building Management Act and maximum occupancy limits, and, where the office employs five or more regular workers, submit the basic workplace safety and health declaration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. No additional industrial fire, hazardous-material, or structural civil-defense permit applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity without a domestic place of business must appoint a tax representative (a person residing in Korea) and file the corporate registration and business registration application with the competent district tax office having jurisdiction over the representative's place of abode. The filing must include the entity's articles of incorporation, the written appointment of a tax representative, a power of attorney, and evidence of the transaction nexus such as a digital service contract. For VAT purposes, the Business Registration Application for a foreign supplier must be submitted before the supply is made; the NTS typically issues a 10-digit registered business number functioning as the TIN/VAT ID within 2-5 business days. Registration can be executed electronically through HomeTax using a bearer certificate or an appointed agent's certificate; where the entity has no Korean IP address or certificate, the tax representative files physically on behalf of the entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a check-the-box classification election; a Chusik Hoesa is automatically subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules are applied under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination and the OECD MLI, but no elective tax classification is available to a non-resident party.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Presidential Decree
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General VAT registration: annual taxable turnover exceeding KRW 10,000,000; for foreign suppliers of electronic services (B2C digital supplies): cumulative annual revenue exceeding KRW 10,000,000 from Korean consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices issued by a Korean supplier or foreign registered supplier are required to be electronic e-tax invoices transmitted in real-time to the NTS electronic tax invoice system (HomeTax) on or before the last day of the month following the supply. B2C foreign digital services are filed in quarterly VAT returns (April 1-30, July 1-25, October 1-25, January 1-25). There is no physical fiscal stamp in Korea; the e-invoice transmission itself acts as the clearance, and the NTS performs anti-fraud matching between e-invoices, VAT returns, and customs transaction data. Failure to transmit triggers additional tax of 0.1%-0.5% of supply value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on the export of goods under Article 21 of the VAT Act and, for services, on services prescribed as export services (foreign exchange earning services), including software and helpdesk services rendered to a non-resident without a Korean place of business, where the supply is used wholly outside Korea and the consideration is paid in foreign currency or in Korean won from a foreign-source account. For a customer-support helpdesk SaaS, the contract must identify the foreign customer, the service usage location, and the remittance of invoices in an approved currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Declaration Acknowledgement) filed and processed through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Commercial invoice / service contract with the non-resident purchaser specifying the nature and type of software/helpdesk service
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation (Exchange Bank Settlement Certificate) evidencing inward remittance in foreign currency or foreign-source Korean won
Service performance evidence such as server logs or jurisdiction-neutral user access records demonstrating that the beneficiary is a foreign entity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, the NTS may conduct retrospective review for up to 5 years. If zero-rating is rejected due to failure to substantiate the export or foreign exchange receipt, VAT is recomputed at 10% output tax with an additional tax for unfaithful returns (10% of the understated tax), or 40% in cases of fraudulent misreporting or document falsification, plus statutory late-payment interest from the due date to the payment date. The taxpayer is also denied any corresponding input VAT credits on related costs, and a criminal referral can be made for tax evasion exceeding statutory thresholds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the implementing authority for the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalized current-account regime but retains a statutory capital-account control framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Bank of Korea, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, administers the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) through authorized foreign exchange banks. For the customer-support helpdesk SaaS Chusik Hoesa, operating income from exported SaaS subscription services is convertible into KRW on a settlement basis without mandatory surrender; however, each receipt must be reported through an authorized bank. Capital receipts, such as paid-in capital from a non-resident parent, are freely convertible only after a foreign-investment report is filed and funds are deposited into a dedicated foreign-currency account; otherwise the remittance is characterized as a borrowing transaction and subject to external-debt regulations. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted once the foreign-invested enterprise registration is complete and corporate taxes, dividend withholding tax, and the foreign investor's resident tax certificate are settled. Practical hurdles include FEIS transaction-code granularity, a 15-month export-proceeds receipt limit, and the requirement that all payments be cleared through a locally licensed foreign exchange bank, which slows cross-border invoice settlement and complicates outsourcing-custody cash flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exported software services and SaaS subscriptions, export proceeds must be received and settled by the domestic exporter within 15 months from the shipment or service-provision completion date. The mandatory receipt proportion is 100% of the invoice value; no currency surrender is required, meaning the exporter may maintain the foreign currency in a domestic foreign-currency account or convert it to KRW at the market rate. Overdue proceeds exceeding 30 days require a delay report to the authorized foreign exchange bank, and unrecovered export amounts after 15 months require Bank of Korea/FEIS approval to avoid administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (USD/KRW) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW)
Capital Escrow Account (USD/KRW) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW)
Capital Escrow Account (USD/KRW) and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking rail. Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Banking Act, only institutions licensed by the Financial Services Commission as banks are permitted to conduct foreign exchange banking and maintain the FEIS reporting identity required for corporate settlement. Foreign digital EMIs and non-bank fintech providers such as Wise or Revolut do not hold a domestic banking license in the Republic of Korea, and therefore cannot legally service the Chusik Hoesa as its main treasury account or capital escrow vehicle. Stripe and PayPal are payment aggregator rails for collecting subscription income, but they must settle to a domestic tier-1 bank account and cannot replace a licensed Korean bank for FX reporting, trade payments, or foreign-investment compliance. Designating an offshore EMI as the principal account would block capital verification, create unreported cross-border clearing, and be rejected by Korean tax and customs authorities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, tier-1 Korean banks require the statutory representative or a locally appointed signatory with authorized power of attorney to appear physically at a domestic branch for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not universally accepted for a commercial operating account; the bank requires the authorized representative's passport, corporate seal exemption confirmation, corporate registry abstracts, and a physical signature under branch supervision. A non-resident director may execute an apostilled power of attorney appointing a Korean-resident joint signatory, but the Korean signatory must still attend the KYC interview in person and verify the corporate seal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain includes a non-resident investor or a Korean-resident director is absent; bank flags lack of transparent local management and operating control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate Registry Extract showing the Chusik Hoesa articles of incorporation and officer list; share register with the complete UBO chain to the ultimate individual; apostilled and notarized passports of all UBOs; Korean tax identification documents; board resolution appointing a Korean-resident general manager or signatory with management authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from the offshore parent is received in multiple tranches without a documented Foreign Investment Promotion Act report, raising suspicion of disguised borrowing or reverse capital flight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report receipt filed with an authorized foreign exchange bank; executed investment or shareholder loan agreement; source-of-funds evidence including six-month investor bank statements and audited financial statements; parent company incorporation documents; board meeting minutes authorizing each tranche; and anti-corruption and sanctioned-party declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SaaS subscription revenue is collected via Stripe and PayPal from diverse global customers and arrives commingled in the operating account, triggering suspicion of unlicensed money transmission or third-party pass-through activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed SaaS subscription agreements and end-user license agreements; customer-country breakdown and customer KYC summaries; Stripe and PayPal merchant settlement reports; invoice and billing-extract files; and a funds-flow reconciliation statement confirming receipts correspond to recognized SaaS subscription liabilities rather than deposit-taking or money transmission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound remittances for IT services, software royalties, or outsourced helpdesk support to overseas group companies materially exceed revenue benchmarks, suggesting profit-shifting and lacking economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service and license agreements describing the exact helpdesk and cloud-support deliverables; transfer pricing documentation and benchmark study; time-tracking and staffing records proving Korean execution; Korean withholding tax certificates for royalty or service remittances; and management accounts demonstrating local headcount, infrastructure, and operational decision-making in the Republic of Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or quasi-equity from the foreign parent must be routed through an authorized foreign exchange bank in Korea using SWIFT MT103. The wire should be denominated in USD or KRW, reference the foreign-investment report number, and carry the FEIS transaction code matching foreign direct investment into a domestic corporation. Funds must first credit a dedicated foreign-investor capital escrow account and then be converted to KRW after the foreign-invested enterprise registration is issued. Capital verification is evidenced by the bank's inward remittance receipt, the FEIS report certificate, and the corporate registry entry for issued shares. A comprehensive cash-flow file must be retained showing investor identity, financing structure, and absence of third-party payment intermediation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine helpdesk and cloud-infrastructure vendor payments should be cleared via standard SWIFT MT103 wires from the operating account using the appropriate service-payment remittance purpose code and the underlying contract reference. For larger infrastructure procurements or imported hardware, Korean banks issue commercial letters of credit (MT700) against a collateralized KRW deposit or bank guarantee, while documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are suitable for established trading counterparties. Domestic operational disbursements, including payroll and local subcontractor payments, must be settled in KRW through the BOK-Wire+ system and should be linked to the corporate bank's digital clearing API to preserve auditability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW) with a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank on documented underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps with a licensed Korean bank for matching the maturities of SaaS export receipts and contracted overseas disbursements
Currency swaps limited to confirmed long-term cross-border service or financing exposures, with mandatory FEIS reporting and no speculative position-taking

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts are restricted for onshore Korean legal entities and should not be booked; all hedging must be executed through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and regular shareholders' meeting approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General meeting of shareholders (corporate records retained at the registered office; no regulatory filing fee for private non-listed companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar year-end Chusik Hoesa, no later than March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the regular shareholders' meeting or to prepare and present annual financial statements exposes the representative director and directors to administrative fines of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,100) under the Commercial Act, plus civil liability for damages caused to shareholders or third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and local corporate income tax return with payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and competent local government through the NTS Hometax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, filing and payment are due by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; under-reporting penalty of 10%; fraudulent understatement penalty of 40%; daily overdue interest of approximately 0.025% per day on unpaid tax. Prolonged non-payment can trigger tax seizure, compulsory collection, closure of the business registration, and, for a dormant company, administrative strike-off from the commercial register after the statutory peremptory notice procedure under Commercial Act Article 520-2.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and submission to the financial regulator (required only when mandatory audit thresholds are met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the fiscal year-end; the independent certified auditor must deliver the audit report before the regular shareholders' meeting, and the company must submit the audit report to the FSC and KICPA within 2 weeks after the report is received and presented to the shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint the required external auditor, refusal to submit the audit report, or obstruction of the audit subjects the company to administrative fines of up to KRW 10 million (approximately USD 7,100); false or negligent audit reporting may lead to criminal penalties, director liability, and disciplinary sanctions imposed by KICPA on the auditor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of the register of members, including any foreign shareholding change report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's registered head office records and, where foreign investment is registered, the designated foreign exchange bank / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing obligation; transfers of registered shares must be recorded in the register of members before the transferee can exercise shareholder rights. Changes to a registered foreign investment must be filed within 30 days from the date of the shareholding transfer or capital change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an accurate register of members may invalidate share transfers against the company and expose directors to administrative fines or civil claims; failure to report foreign investment changes within 30 days may result in administrative fines and loss of foreign-investment protections.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies applies to: (i) all listed companies on KOSPI or KOSDAQ; (ii) non-listed stock companies with total assets of at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.6 million) at the fiscal year-end; (iii) financial companies subject to FSC supervisory audit rules; and (iv) such other companies designated by the Financial Services Commission or Presidential Decree because of public-interest status, public securities issuance, or a designated audit order under Article 6 of the Act. The general private non-public Chusik Hoesa threshold is exclusively balance-sheet based; turnover and headcount are not standalone general audit triggers absent FSC designation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korea-adopted International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for listed and financial companies; non-listed companies subject to external audit may apply K-GAAP; eligible small and medium-sized entities apply the Korean SME Accounting Standards (K-SME Accounting Standards). All frameworks are issued by the Korea Accounting Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a separate annual UBO franchise filing for a private Chusik Hoesa. The annual UBO confirmation occurs through the shareholders' meeting, the board's review of the register of members, and the mandatory attachment of the current shareholding structure to the corporate tax return. Any transfer of shares must be recorded in the register of members to be effective against the company; a transferor or transferee must request the registration without undue delay. For foreign-invested companies, any change in the foreign shareholding percentages or foreign direct investment registration must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank and MOTIE within 30 days from the transfer. The company must also maintain adequate customer due diligence records of beneficial owners if it acts as a financial or payment intermediary, but ordinary Chusik Hoesa entities are not required to file an annual UBO return with the commercial registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,800 per year for a commercial registered office address and corporate secretarial support in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 30,000 per annual certified audit for a company above the KRW 12 billion mandatory audit threshold; USD 0 for a company below all statutory audit thresholds unless FSC-designated

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on taxable income above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% on taxable income above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% on taxable income above KRW 300 billion. A 10% local income tax surcharge is additionally imposed on the national corporate tax payable, and a further 10% national surcharge applies to the portion of taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion for certain large corporations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Certified venture enterprises may obtain a 50% reduction of corporate income tax for 5 years; R&D credits of 15% to 50% apply for qualifying technology development, with enhanced rates for national strategic technologies; job creation and employment expansion tax credits are available; an early-stage venture tax deduction applies to newly established venture startups; foreign-invested enterprises in qualifying free economic zones and foreign investment zones may receive 100% exemption for 7 years and 50% reduction for the following 3 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; special provisions also permit accelerated depreciation and reserves for overseas market development.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Payable Return (Statutory Corporate Tax Return Form, National Tax Service Form No. 30) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr), together with the financial statements, tax base adjustment schedules, balance sheet, income statement, and the Report on International Transactions where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. For fiscal years ending on 31 December, the annual tax return is filed once per year, accompanied by two interim prepayments; interim prepayments are calculated on the basis of one half of the previous year's tax payable and are due within two months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year (i.e., by 31 August for a calendar-year company), and the final settlement is made with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by 31 March of the following year for a calendar-year corporation). Where the corporation is subject to statutory external audit, the deadline for filing the financial statements accompanying the tax return can be extended by up to 180 days; however, the tax amount shown in the preliminary return must be paid by the original statutory deadline, and the tax payable as finally determined must be paid by the extended filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ten-digit corporate business registration number issued by the Korean tax office upon incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean business registration number and the foreign investment registration certificate number if the company is registered as a foreign-invested enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Corporate Name, Representative Director and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax base type classification, fiscal year end, date of incorporation and representative director details of the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact legal name in the Korean commercial registration; indicate whether the entity is a resident corporation with domestic management or a foreign corporation with a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Type of Business and Industry Classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of business activities including ISIC 6201 computer programming and related activities and NAICS 511210 software publishing, specifically multi-channel omni-helpdesk and conversational bot cloud services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the applicable small and medium enterprise (SME) indicators and the software-as-a-service business sub-classification; these codes affect R&D credit ceilings and tax rate application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Business Place and Secondary Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of the head office, branch offices, and any overseas permanent establishment of the Korean entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For branch operations of a foreign corporation, report the Korean permanent establishment address and the foreign head office address separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Net Income (Loss) per Financial Statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax determined under the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or General Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust the branch net income to the domestic source income as recorded in the Korean permanent establishment ledger; book-to-tax differences must be itemized in the adjustment schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses disallowed by the Corporate Income Tax Act, including entertainment expenses over the statutory ceiling, fines and penalties, certain donations, accrued non-business interest, and expenses lacking tax invoices or supporting vouchers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing adjustment add-backs and expenses recharacterized as non-business expenses by the tax office; cross-border technology service fees must have proper contracts and withholding evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Deductible Adjustments and Tax-Exempt Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of items such as dividend income gross-up relief, reserves for bad debts, non-taxable domestic dividends, and the offset of loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward of 5 years applies; the deduction may not exceed 80% of taxable income before deduction in any given year for loss carryforwards recognized after 2017.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after book-to-tax adjustments and loss offset, used as the base for the progressive corporate tax rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign corporations, the tax base covers Korean domestic source income attributable to the permanent establishment, including services rendered in Korea, and is computed under the same adjustment rules as resident corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the progressive rates of 9%, 19%, 21% and 24% to the corresponding tax base brackets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The same progressive schedule applies; non-resident corporations are not subject to the additional surplus tax on undistributed profits that applies to certain personal-close corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of R&D tax credits, venture enterprise reductions, foreign tax credits, interim prepayments, withholding tax credits, and tax credit for job creation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are allowed only for foreign taxes paid on foreign source income included in the Korean tax base and only to the extent of the Korean tax on that income; carryforward of unused foreign tax credit is limited to 5 years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Final Tax Payable and Local Income Tax Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax after credits plus the 10% local income tax surcharge, and the amount of tax due with the return or refund to be credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local income tax surcharge is 10% of the national corporate tax and applies to non-resident permanent establishments equally; payment is made in a single wire transfer to the national and local tax collection accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Attachment A - Financial Statements and External Audit Report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, cash flow statement, notes, and the independent auditor's opinion where required by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (assets exceeding approximately KRW 12 billion).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The branch financial statements must be certified by a Korean certified public accountant if the branch revenue and asset thresholds are met; the Korean branch accounts must separately reflect home office allocations of general and administrative expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Attachment B - Report on International Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report on related-party cross-border transactions including sales, purchases, royalties, loans, service fees and interest paid to or received from foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory attachment for any year in which reportable international transactions with foreign related parties occur; detailed Local File preparation is triggered at the KRW 5 billion threshold and the Master File at the KRW 100 billion revenue and KRW 10 billion transaction threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or false filing of the annual corporate income tax return attracts a negligence penalty of 10% of the unpaid tax for general underreporting and 20% of the unpaid tax for fraudulent underreporting or non-filing; in addition, a daily delinquency surcharge is imposed on the unpaid national and local income tax, calculated at the statutory rate of the base interest rate plus 3 percentage points (approximately 0.022% per day in 2024); failure to attach the Report on International Transactions triggers an administrative fine of up to KRW 30 million; where the tax office determines tax by official assessment, penalties and interest accrue from the original due date, and criminal referral is made for cases involving fraudulent evasion.
